# Professional experience

This portfolio is a curated, evidence-led overview of selected work across scientific research, software development, Data Science, and AI evaluation. It connects problems, methods, implementation, and results; it is not intended to replace the full employment chronology on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brunjm/), which remains the reference for exact employer dates and official role titles.

My path spans research-laboratory work, startup/product development, software consulting, and software-vendor environments. The through-line is multidisciplinary problem solving: translating a domain question into a model or method, implementing it, and evaluating the result.

## Research and scientific modelling

**Thesis research — TODO(date) (thesis/publication milestone: 2007).** My thesis work concerned reduced-complexity mathematical models for environmental transport and atmospheric dispersion. It connects applied mathematics and partial differential equations with model identification and numerical reasoning.

- [Thesis record: *Modèles à complexité réduite de transport pour applications environnementales*](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226478979_Reduced-Order_Modelling_of_Dispersion)
- [2006 paper: *Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite*](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/)
- [2008 chapter: *Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion*](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14)

**Postdoctoral research — TODO(date) (TEB-Veg paper published in 2018).** This work concerns the modelling of urban hydrological processes and their representation in the Town Energy Balance model. The paper is a concrete link between mathematical modelling, environmental processes, numerical simulation, and a maintained scientific model.

- [2018 peer-reviewed paper: *Improvements to the hydrological processes of the Town Energy Balance model (TEB-Veg, SURFEX v7.3) for urban modelling and impact assessment*](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/11/4175/2018/)
- [Official CNRM overview of TEB](https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/teb-town-energy-balance/)
- [Official SURFEX overview](https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/surfex-2/)
- [TEB model source repository](https://github.com/teb-model/teb)

The institutional context includes [Cemagref → IRSTEA → INRAE (institutional history)](https://www.inrae.fr/sites/jobs/files/guide_accueil_-_juillet_2023_-_web.pdf) and [IFSTTAR and its integration into Université Gustave Eiffel](https://www.univ-gustave-eiffel.fr/luniversite/notre-projet). These links provide institutional context; the publications above are the evidence for the scientific work.

**Scientific methods and technology:** applied mathematics, partial differential equations, reduced-order modelling, fluid mechanics, atmospheric dispersion, environmental hydrology, numerical simulation, Fortran, and SURFEX–TEB.

### Qlik

**Employment dates:** TODO(date) (five years of Data Science work reported in the Qlik/Talend lab).

**Technology areas:** Python, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon SageMaker.

**Work areas:** data analysis and statistics, classical machine learning, LLM/NLP and generative AI, experimentation, benchmarks, model evaluation, and Python development/industrialisation.

One industrial project involved a state-of-the-art review, then the creation of an independent pipeline and benchmark for hallucination detection. Using Amazon Bedrock, the work evaluated an AWS guardrail-based approach against state-of-the-art small language models (SLMs), with a common evaluation workflow and analysis of metrics, thresholds, and errors. Public disclosure is limited to methodology and qualitative comparative observations: Qlik/Talend has not authorised publication of aggregate numerical results, and internal code, data, architecture details, and other proprietary information are excluded.

## The common thread

Across these contexts, the recurring work is to understand a domain problem, select a method that fits its constraints, implement or integrate a solution, and evaluate whether it behaves as intended. The combination of scientific modelling, software engineering, and Data Science is the main thread—not any single language or framework.
